mainTopic: How a man's status as a כהן is established: a casual remark, receiving תרומה or מעשר ראשון, a share received in בית דין, and the testimony of one witness
overview: The גמרא first explains how a brother's word can count: it works when he speaks casually (מסיח לפי תומו). It backs this up with a story about a man who casually remembered being immersed as a child to eat תרומה, and רבי accepted him as a כהן on that basis. Next, a ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says that receiving מעשר ראשון, like תרומה, creates a חזקה of כהונה. The גמרא explains this through רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view that a כהן may also get מעשר ראשון, and through עזרא's penalty that took it away from the לויים. רב חסדא then limits the ruling to the son of a known כהן who received an official share at the threshing floor. That share shows he is not a חלל. רב ששת explains that a share 'in בית דין' means inheriting תרומה with brothers, which proves nothing, because a חלל may own it to sell. Finally, the גמרא asks how רבן שמעון בן גמליאל differs from רבי אליעזר in the משנה about one witness. It rejects one answer and begins describing a new case, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The brother spoke casually
steps.stepSummary: The brother's statement counts because he said it casually, not as formal testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about a case where he spoke offhandedly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier question: how can a brother's statement help establish a person's family status? It says the brother mentioned it casually.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who is just talking, not trying to prove anything, has no reason to make things up. So his words are trusted even though he is a relative and is not giving formal testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: Speaking offhandedly, innocently, without intending to testify

steps.confusionAlert: This step is an answer to a question asked just before this section begins. It is not a new topic.

phrases.english: In a case where he speaks offhandedly.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמֵסִיחַ לְפִי תּוּמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this section about how a brother's statement can help.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case to casual speech
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A brother's statement might seem to have no value, since a relative cannot testify.
steps.terutzMaskana: A casual, unplanned remark is trusted.

steps.title: The story of the man who remembered eating תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, tells of a man who casually recalled being immersed as a child so he could eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: A man was talking casually and said, "I remember when I was a child riding on my father's shoulder. They took me out of school, took off my shirt, and immersed me so I could eat תרומה that evening."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to show that casual speech is trusted in questions of כהונה. The man's memory shows his family treated him as a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a כהן may eat תרומה, and he must be טהור to do so. The man was not trying to prove anything. He was just telling a childhood memory, and that memory showed his family's priestly status.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן; only כהנים may eat it
They immersed me (in a מקוה) to make me טהור
School, where young children learn

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Like that which Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
There was an incident with one man
who was speaking offhandedly, and said:
I remember when I was a child
and riding on my father's shoulder,
and they took me out of school,
and they took off my shirt,
and they immersed me
so I could eat teruma in the evening.
phrases.notes: Only a כהן may eat תרומה, so this memory shows his family were כהנים.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real case of casual speech to support the answer in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That casual speech is trusted to establish כהונה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story told by רב יהודה in the name of שמואל

steps.title: רבי חייא's ending: רבי made him a כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא adds the end of the story: the man's friends called him 'יוחנן who eats חלות,' and רבי accepted him as a כהן based on his words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא finishes the story: "My friends kept away from me and called me 'יוחנן who eats חלות.'" And רבי raised him to כהונה based on what he said.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא adds the end of the story, and that ending is the key to the proof. רבי actually ruled that the man was a כהן because of his casual remark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this ending, the story is only a memory. With it, we see a real ruling: רבי יהודה הנשיא relied on a casual statement to declare someone a כהן. This shows that a casual remark has real legal weight.

keyTerms.meaning: Completes it, adds the ending of the story
Challah portions, given to a כהן and eaten only by כהנים
Raised him to priestly status, ruled that he is a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: A casual remark (מסיח לפי תומו) can be enough to establish that someone is a כהן. רבי actually ruled this way.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling that makes the story a proof for the answer in step 1.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiya ends the story with:
And my friends kept away from me,
and they would call me
'Yochanan who eats challot.'
phrases.notes: Like תרומה, חלה goes to a כהן, so the nickname shows he ate priestly food.

phrases.english: And Rebbi raised him to the status of a kohen based on his word.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא מְסַיֵּים בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story from step 2 with the ruling that turns it into a proof.
steps.raayaObject: That a casual statement is accepted to establish כהונה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי's ruling in the story, as completed by רבי חייא

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: first tithe also proves priesthood
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: receiving מעשר ראשון, like receiving תרומה, shows a person is a כהן. But receiving a share in בית דין does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Just as receiving תרומה is a חזקה (presumption) of כהונה, so too receiving מעשר ראשון is a חזקה of כהונה. But someone who receives a share in בית דין does not get a חזקה from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic. It quotes a ברייתא about which gifts, when someone receives them, show that he is a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds מעשר ראשון to the list of gifts that create a חזקה of כהונה. It also gives a limit: a share handed out in בית דין does not prove anything.

keyTerms.meaning: A presumption (assumed status) that the person is a כהן
First tithe, a tenth of the produce, normally given to a לוי
One who receives a share when it is distributed in court
It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Just as teruma is a presumption of priesthood,
so too first tithe is a presumption of priesthood,
but one who receives a share in court,
it is not a presumption.
phrases.notes: Getting a share handed out in בית דין does not prove that he is a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: which gifts create a חזקה of כהונה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Receiving מעשר ראשון creates a חזקה of כהונה, just like תרומה. A share received in בית דין does not.

steps.title: But מעשר ראשון goes to a לוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: מעשר ראשון is given to a לוי, so how can it prove someone is a כהן?
steps.simpleTranslation: But מעשר ראשון belongs to a לוי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. Receiving a לוי's gift should not show that someone is a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מעשר ראשון is the gift of the לויים, then receiving it should at most show that someone is a לוי. It should not show that he is a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: A member of the tribe of לוי who is not a כהן

phrases.english: First tithe belongs to a Levite!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן דְּלֵוִי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that מעשר ראשון is a חזקה of כהונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מעשר ראשון is given to a לוי, so receiving it cannot show that someone is a כהן.

steps.title: This follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who holds that מעשר ראשון may be given to a כהן as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. As a ברייתא teaches: תרומה goes to a כהן and מעשר ראשון to a לוי; these are the words of רבי עקיבא. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: מעשר ראשון may go to a כהן too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds like the תנא who says a כהן may also receive מעשר ראשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא gives מעשר ראשון only to a לוי. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says it may also be given to a כהן. According to his view, a כהן can receive מעשר ראשון, so the ברייתא's ruling makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: To a כהן as well
The words of, the opinion of

phrases.english: It follows Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.
As it was taught in a baraita:
Teruma goes to a kohen,
first tithe to a Levite;
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
First tithe goes to a kohen as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה. דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by connecting the ברייתא to a specific תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the ruling to a specific opinion among the תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מעשר ראשון belongs only to a לוי, so it cannot show כהונה.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, a כהן may also receive מעשר ראשון.

steps.title: But a לוי can still receive it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה only said 'a כהן too'. He never said a לוי cannot receive it. So receiving it still does not prove כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said 'to a כהן as well.' But did he say it goes to a כהן and not to a לוי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer. Even under רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, a לוי still receives מעשר ראשון. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To prove someone is a כהן, the gift must be one that only a כהן gets. Since both a כהן and a לוי can receive מעשר ראשון, receiving it does not tell us which one he is.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, granted that
Did he say...? (a rhetorical challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה added the כהן. He did not remove the לוי. That is exactly why this challenge works.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימוֹר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה ״אַף לְכֹהֵן״,
phrases.english: Granted that Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said 'to a kohen as well,'
did he say to a kohen and not to a Levite?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימוֹר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, a לוי can also receive מעשר ראשון. So receiving it cannot single someone out as a כהן.

steps.title: After עזרא's penalty, only כהנים received מעשר ראשון
steps.stepSummary: Yes, receiving מעשר ראשון proves כהונה, because after עזרא penalized the לויים it was given only to כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, it proves he is a כהן. This is after עזרא penalized them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the pushback from step 7. It says that in practice, מעשר ראשון was given only to כהנים after עזרא penalized the לויים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said a לוי can still get מעשר ראשון, so getting it proves nothing. The answer is that עזרא's penalty took it away from the לויים. From then on, anyone receiving it is assumed to be a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
A penalty / he penalized them
עזרא the scribe, who led the return from בבל

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how the ברייתא from step 4 can treat מעשר ראשון just like תרומה as proof of כהונה.

phrases.english: Yes, after Ezra penalized them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the לויים. עזרא penalized them for not coming up from בבל, so the מעשר went to כהנים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, בָּתַר דְּקַנְסִינְהוּ עֶזְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical decree changes who actually receives
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a לוי may also receive מעשר ראשון, receiving it proves nothing
steps.terutzMaskana: After עזרא's penalty, only כהנים received it, so it does show כהונה

steps.title: Maybe they gave it to him by chance
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps he was really a לוי and they just happened to give him the מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it just happened that they gave it to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects again. Even after עזרא's decree, maybe someone happened to give the מעשר to a לוי anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עזרא's penalty sets the usual practice, but people do not always follow it. So one case of receiving מעשר could be a random exception, and it would prove nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps / maybe
It happened by chance

phrases.english: But perhaps it happened that they gave it to him!
phrases.notes: He means: maybe the man is really a לוי, and someone just gave him the מעשר anyway.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא אִיקְּרוּ וְיָהֲבוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that receiving מעשר ראשון proves כהונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single case of receiving could be a chance gift to a לוי

steps.title: רב חסדא: The father is a known כהן and the son's status is rumored
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא sets up a case where the father is a known כהן and there is a rumor that the son is a חלל. The son then received מעשר at the threshing floor. Being a לוי is ruled out, so the only question is whether he is a בן גרושה or a בן חלוצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: What case are we dealing with? A case where we know this man's father is a כהן. A rumor went out that the son is the son of a divorced woman or a חלוצה, and they gave him himself a share of מעשר at the threshing floors. Could he be a לוי? He is not a לוי. So what worry is left? Only that he is a בן גרושה or a בן חלוצה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the 'by chance' worry by describing a case where the son cannot be a לוי, because his father is a known כהן. The only doubt is whether he is a חלל, and this sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry 'maybe he is a לוי' is gone, since the father is a כהן. The real question is whether the son is a kosher כהן or a חלל, who counts as a regular ישראל. The next step explains why getting an official share answers that question.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here?
Has an established status
A rumor
Son of a divorcee or a חלוצה married to a כהן, so he is a חלל
The threshing floors, where the produce was given out

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
With what are we dealing here?
Such as where it is established to us about this man's father
that he is a priest,
and a rumor went out about him
phrases.notes: "Him" here is the son, not the father.

phrases.english: that he is the son of a divorcee or the son of a chalutza,
and they gave him himself a share
of tithe at the threshing floors.
A Levite? He is not a Levite,
so what is there to say?

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן גְּרוּשָׁה אוֹ בֶּן חֲלוּצָה הוּא.
phrases.english: That he is the son of a divorcee or the son of a chalutza.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by limiting the ברייתא to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The receiver might be a לוי who got it by chance
steps.terutzMaskana: The father is a known כהן, so the only doubt is whether the son is a חלל

steps.title: Even if זרים may eat מעשר, no one gives them an official share
steps.stepSummary: Some say a non-כהן may not have מעשר ראשון at all. Others say he may eat it if he is fed it. Either way, no one gives him an official share at the threshing floor, so getting such a share shows he is a kosher כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Clearly, according to the one who says מעשר ראשון is forbidden to זרים, they would not have given it to him. But even according to the one who says מעשר ראשון is permitted to זרים, that only means someone may feed it to them. As an official share, they do not give it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב חסדא's answer. It explains why an official share at the threshing floor proves the son is not a חלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מעשר is forbidden to זרים, a חלל would never get it. Even if זרים may eat it, that only means a כהן who already has it can hand some to them. Giving out an official share is only for real כהנים, so the son is shown to be a kosher כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: It goes without saying
Non-כהנים
To feed
As an official share

steps.whatToRemember: Receiving מעשר at the threshing floor proves כהונה because, after עזרא, official shares went only to kosher כהנים.
steps.confusionAlert: Being allowed to eat something is not the same as being handed an official share. Only the official share proves status.

phrases.english: It is not necessary to say, according to the one who says
first tithe is forbidden to non-priests,
that they would not have given it to him.
But even according to the one who says
first tithe is permitted to non-priests,
that applies only to feeding it to them,
phrases.notes: A כהן who already got the מעשר may give some to a non-כהן to eat.

phrases.english: but as an official share
they do not give it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא מִיבַּעְיָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן אָסוּר לְזָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב חסדא's answer from step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Telling apart being allowed to eat from receiving an official share
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If זרים may eat מעשר ראשון, a חלל could have received it
steps.terutzMaskana: An official share at the threshing floor is given only to kosher כהנים

steps.title: If בית דין does not prove status, what does?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא's line that a share in בית דין is not a proof, and asks how that can be.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says: one who receives a share in בית דין does not get a presumed status. If it is not a presumption in court, where would it be one?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the second half of the ברייתא from step 4. It is puzzled, since a court is where things are checked most carefully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You would think that something given out in בית דין is the strongest proof of all. So the ברייתא's statement seems backwards, and it needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: One who receives a share
Court
Presumed status

phrases.english: And one who receives a share in court
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the ברייתא from step 4.

phrases.english: it is not a presumption.

phrases.aramaic: אִי בְּבֵית דִּין לָא הָוְיָא חֲזָקָה,
phrases.english: If in court it is not a presumption,
where is it a presumption?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בְּבֵית דִּין לָא הָוְיָא חֲזָקָה, הֵיכָא הָוְיָא חֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a new clause of the ברייתא from step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that a share in בית דין is not a proof
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בית דין is the most reliable setting, so it should give the strongest proof

steps.title: רב ששת: It means inheriting תרומה with brothers
steps.stepSummary: רב שׁשׁת explains that the ברייתא is talking about splitting up a father's estate, including תרומה, among brothers in court.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שׁשׁת said: This is what it means. One who takes a share of תרומה from his father's property, together with his brothers in court, does not get a presumed status.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שׁשׁת explains the puzzling line. The court here is dividing an inheritance, and it is not checking anyone's family line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the court divides an estate, every son gets his part of the property, including any תרומה. A חלל can own תרומה even if he may not eat it. So his share tells us nothing about whether he is a kosher כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means
His father's property
The portion of produce given to כהנים

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: This is what it is saying:
One who takes a share of terumah in his father's property
with his brothers in court,
it is not a presumption.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A share in בית דין means the court gave him priestly gifts
steps.terutzMaskana: It means dividing an inheritance, which says nothing about lineage

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs to teach something so obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא bothers to say that inheriting תרומה does not prove כהונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An inheritance just passes on property, so of course it proves nothing about lineage. The גמרא wants to know what new idea the ברייתא is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ruling as רב שׁשׁת explained it
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שׁשׁת's reading of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An inheritance clearly proves nothing about lineage, so why teach it?

steps.title: The brothers eat it, but he may only sell it
steps.stepSummary: You might have thought that since his brothers take the תרומה to eat, he does too. The ברייתא teaches that he may be taking it only to sell.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since those brothers take it to eat, this one also takes it to eat. So it teaches us: those take it to eat, and this one takes it to sell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new idea in the ruling. Getting the same share as kosher כהן brothers does not mean he gets to eat it the way they do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since all the brothers get the same thing, you might think they all have the same status. But a חלל may own תרומה and sell it to a כהן, even though he may not eat it. So his share does not prove he is a kosher כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said
It teaches us
For eating
To sell

steps.whatToRemember: A share of תרומה in an inheritance proves nothing. A חלל son may own it and sell it, even though he may not eat it.

phrases.english: You might have said:
since those take it for eating,
phrases.notes: "Those" are the other brothers, who are kosher כהנים.

phrases.english: this one also takes it for eating,
so it teaches us:
those take it for eating,
and this one takes it to sell.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: מִדְּהָנָךְ לַאֲכִילָה, הַאי נָמֵי לַאֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: blocking a mistaken conclusion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Getting the same share as his brothers means he eats it like them
steps.terutzMaskana: He may be taking it only to sell, so it proves nothing about his status

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about one witness for כהונה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the start of the משנה's argument: רבי יהודה says we do not raise someone to כהונה on the word of one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: we do not raise someone to כהונה based on one witness, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening a new topic by quoting the משנה. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'and so on' point to the rest of the משנה: רבי אליעזר says one witness is enough when no one challenges, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says one witness is enough. The גמרא is about to compare these last two views.

keyTerms.meaning: We raise someone to the status of a כהן (let him eat תרומה and so on)
One witness
And so on: the rest of the quote is understood

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One does not elevate a man to priesthood
on the basis of one witness, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה, where רבי אליעזר and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל give their views.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵין מַעֲלִין לִכְהוּנָּה עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section, moving from the תרומה-share discussion to the next part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: one witness is not enough to raise a man to כהונה.

steps.title: Aren't רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר saying the same thing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view seems the same as רבי אליעזר's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is the same as רבי אליעזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. Two תנאים seem to say the same thing, so why list them as two opinions?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says one witness is enough when there is no challenge. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says one witness is enough. Plainly he also means a case with no challenge, so there seems to be no argument between them.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as (used to ask why two views are listed separately)
A תנא in the משנה who holds one witness is enough
A תנא in the משנה who holds one witness is enough when there is no challenge

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
is the same as Rabbi Eliezer!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַיְינוּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה listing רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר as separate opinions.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both allow one witness when no one challenges, so there is no visible difference between them.

steps.title: A suggested difference: can one witness make a challenge?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests they argue about whether a challenge by one witness counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say they differ about a challenge by one witness: רבי אליעזר holds one witness is enough to make a challenge, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds a challenge needs two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer: the two תנאים differ about how many witnesses it takes to make an ערער. This answer is about to be rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this idea, for רבי אליעזר one witness who objects already counts as a challenge, so one supporting witness is not enough. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל one objector is ignored, so one supporting witness still works.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (brings a possible answer, often rejected)
A challenge to someone's lineage
There is a difference between them
One / two

phrases.english: And if you would say
that a challenge by one witness is the difference between them,
that Rabbi Eliezer holds a challenge can be made by one,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סָבַר: עַרְעָר תְּרֵי.
phrases.english: and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds: a challenge needs two.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא עַרְעָר חַד אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the question in step 17.
steps.terutzMaskana: They might differ on whether one witness can make a challenge. This is rejected in the next step.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: everyone agrees a challenge needs two
steps.stepSummary: The suggested difference fails, because רבי יוחנן says all agree a challenge needs at least two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוחנן said: everyone agrees there is no challenge with fewer than two witnesses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggested answer by quoting רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everyone, including רבי אליעזר, holds that one objector is not a real challenge, then the two תנאים cannot be arguing about that. The original question returns: how do they differ?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (brings a source against what was just said)
Everyone agrees
Fewer than two

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
Everyone agrees
there is no challenge with fewer than two!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל, אֵין עַרְעָר פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer offered in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion that the תנאים differ about a one-witness challenge.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוחנן says all agree that a challenge needs two witnesses, so no one holds one witness is enough.

steps.title: A new case: a known כהן's son who was taken down by a rumor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets the argument in a special case: the father is a known כהן, a rumor said the son was a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה, he was taken down, and then one witness says he is a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what case are we dealing with here? The father of this man is known to us as a כהן. A rumor spread that the son is a בן גרושה or a בן חלוצה, so we took him down from כהונה. Then one witness came and said: I know he is a כהן...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the failed answer and begins describing a specific case where the two תנאים can disagree. The description keeps going in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is no longer about the number of challengers. It is about a son of a known כהן who was lowered only because of a rumor, and whether one witness can now restore him. The case is still being built, and the ruling comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? (sets the opinions in a specific case)
Known and established as having a certain status
A rumor
Son of a divorced woman and a כהן, who is a חלל and not a fit כהן
Son of a woman who had חליצה and a כהן, who is also not a fit כהן
We brought him down from his status

steps.confusionAlert: The rumor is about the son, not the father. The father stays a known כהן; the question is whether the son is from a forbidden marriage.

phrases.english: Rather, with what case are we dealing here?
Where the father of this man is established to us
as a priest,
and a rumor went out about him

phrases.aramaic: דְּבֶן גְּרוּשָׁה אוֹ בֶּן חֲלוּצָה הוּא,
phrases.english: that he is the son of a divorced woman or the son of a chalutza,
and we downgraded him.
And one witness came and said:
I know about him that he is a priest,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 19 rejected the first answer, this gives a new answer to the question in step 17 by setting up a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Placing the argument in a specific case (הכא במאי עסקינן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two תנאים differ about whether one witness can make a challenge, which was rejected.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ in a case where a known כהן's son was lowered because of a rumor and one witness supports him. The full ruling continues in the next lines.
